findings.finding: The plan's central codebase-external assertion — 'Local evidence recorded on the ticket confirms pipx 1.16.5 exposes `--backend {pip,uv}`' — is unverifiable: the only accessible linked ticket (b7a2-4453-3bbd-4a54) contains no mention of `--backend pip`, pipx 1.16.5, or any captured `pipx install --help` output; the client report archive lives on an operator host outside the repo; no repo artifact (fixture, script, or doc) stores a `pipx --help` capture; and `resolve_symbol` cannot confirm the flag. Because AC1 and AC2 both encode `--backend pip` as grep targets that must pass, the workaround command baked into the README and both ACs rests entirely on this unbacked claim.
findings.location: Approach paragraph 3 ('Local evidence recorded on the ticket confirms pipx 1.16.5 exposes `--backend {pip,uv}`'); AC2 (`grep -Fq -- "--backend pip" README.md`)
scenarios: If `--backend pip` was introduced in pipx after 1.16.5 or spelled differently (e.g. `--pip-args` or via env var), the documented workaround will silently fail for the user it targets.
AC2's grep passes mechanically once the string is written, regardless of whether the command actually works — a false negative gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the plan: capture `pipx install --help` on a host with pipx 1.16.5 installed and paste the relevant `--backend` line as inline evidence in the Approach, OR cite the pipx changelog entry (e.g. pipx GitHub release notes) that introduced `--backend`. If the flag name or invocation differs, correct it in both the Approach and AC2 before landing.

findings.finding: The plan's sole verification artifact for the `pipx install --backend pip` flag — 'Local evidence recorded on the ticket confirms pipx 1.16.5 exposes `--backend {pip,uv}`' — does not exist in the referenced ticket (b7a2-4453-3bbd-4a54), which contains no pipx --help output. The flag name `--backend` appears nowhere in repo source files and `pipx` is unresolvable in the installed environment. Because `--backend pip` is baked verbatim into the workaround command AND into AC2's grep check, an incorrect flag name means the committed README documents a broken workaround while both ACs silently pass.
findings.location: Approach — 'Local evidence recorded on the ticket confirms pipx 1.16.5 exposes `--backend {pip,uv}`'; AC2: `grep -Fq -- "--backend pip" README.md`
scenarios: If `--backend` is named differently in the installed pipx version (e.g. `--pip-args`, `--installer`, or is a newer-version-only flag), the committed README callout documents a broken workaround and AC2 passes on the wrong text.
A user on an affected host who follows the documented workaround receives 'no such option: --backend' instead of a fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `pipx install --help 2>&1 | grep -i backend` on the host where the workaround was discovered and paste the relevant line into the ticket as a pinned artifact. If the flag is confirmed, add a note like '(verified against pipx 1.16.5 `--help`)' in the plan. evidence: Plan Approach: 'Add a troubleshooting callout in README.md section `### From source`, immediately after its source-install commands.' — no sentence explains why this section over a dedicated troubleshooting page or the PyPI section.

The current `### From source` section (README.md lines 283–292) contains only `pip install` commands, not any `pipx install <local-path>` form, so the rationale for anchoring a pipx troubleshooting note there is non-obvious and goes unexplained.
findings.finding: The plan asserts WHERE to place the callout (`### From source`, immediately after source-install commands) but states no positive rationale for WHY that section is preferred — e.g. that it is the only section where a local-path `pipx install <path>` user would look, or that a dedicated troubleshooting doc would be over-engineered for a single note. The rubric requires the plan to state a positive rationale for the chosen approach; its absence is a MINOR gap.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Add a troubleshooting callout in README.md section `### From source`, immediately after its source-install commands.'
scenarios: An implementer uncertain about placement might instead put the callout in the PyPI section (which does show `pipx install nava-rebar`) because that section already has pipx context, contradicting the plan's intent.
A reviewer of the resulting PR cannot verify the placement choice was deliberate without the stated rationale.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach paragraph, after 'immediately after its source-install commands', add: 'This section is the natural landing point because a user who cloned the repo and ran `pipx install <path>[agents]` will look here first; a separate troubleshooting doc would be disproportionate for a single, narrow note.'
